content:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a regresssion on the TP+PP job (long seqs) after last autoscaler change. p99 token latency ~3x for some requests. Attaching quick profiling output below. Anyone else hit NVLink <-> PCIe cross-hop weirdness?

infra-bot: autoscaler: pods scheduled across different PCIe domains on node-cluster-7 (pack-policy=v2) :warning:

aj: can you paste the flame graph or pprof slice? suspect all-reduce wait or kernel fallback.

maria: minimal profiling below (wall %) from a single request trace — this is after runtime change that updated kernel selection heuristic:
```
compute_forward: 42%
allreduce_wait: 28%
kv_cache_lookup: 10%
kv_cache_miss_recompute: 9%
batching_overhead: 6%
other: 5%
```

chris: interesting — runtime logs show we fell back to a generic attention kernel on hot paths: `selected_kernel=fused_attn_generic` instead of `fused_attn_nvlink_opt`. The fallback occurred because the topology probe reported >1 cross-node hop for some tensor shards. log snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T12:01:23Z] topo_probe: nvlink_local=false pcie_hops=2 prefer_kernel=false
[2026-03-15T12:01:23Z] kernel_select: picked fused_attn_generic (est_latency +18%)
```

yuki: also saw KV cache eviction spike in the same timeframe — shard mapping changed so prefix cache now misses more often. Misses *amplify* compute cost because we re-materialize KV rather than pull from local NVLink cache.

samir: can repro locally with a small rig. hypothesis: autoscaler spread + pack-policy=v2 -> placement across PCIe domains -> kernel heuristic choosing safer generic kernel -> increased allreduce + mem copy -> >p99. We should test a placement policy that prefers NVLink adjacency for PP groups.

aj: quick experiment suggestion: force kernel selection override to nvlink_opt and run canary on the cluster. If latency drops, we know heuristic is too conservative. But be careful: if topology truly splits, forcing nvlink kernel could corrupt performance.

chris: created a small runtime patch to log topology fingerprint and kernel decision more verbosely. also added a toggle `--kernel-force=nvlink_opt` for canary. pushing to canary namespace now.

maria: thanks. also trying a complementary change: reduce KV shard spread to keep KV cache local to PP micro-shard. config snippet I used:
```yaml
placement_policy:
  prefer_nvlink_adjacency: true
  max_shard_spread: 1  # keep KV shards within same NVLink grouping
kernel:
  selection_safe_margin: 0.02  # lower conservatism for canary
```

infra-bot: canary deploy started for runtime-canary-42 on cluster-7 at 2009990087

yuki: initial canary numbers look promising — p99 dropped ~30% and kv_cache_miss rate halved after placement tweak. still seeing small allreduce spikes at larger batch sizes.

aj: can you dump NCCL profiler around the spike? looking for unexpected PCIe transfers or fallback to ring algorithm.

maria: NCCL trace attached (short):
```
NCCL op allreduce size=4MB time=2.8ms path=nvlink->pcie->nvlink (3 hops)
NCCL op allreduce size=8MB time=5.4ms path=nvlink->nvlink (1 hop)
```

chris: that 3-hop path means the scheduler routed one rank over a PCIe bridge mid-way. That's enough to make kernel selection pessimistic. We need topology-aware placement at the pod-scheduler level or a runtime fallback that tries to remap shards onto local NVLink peers before selecting kernel.

samir: proposal: add a cheap preflight: for a serving job, run a micro-probe between planned ranks for NVLink adjacency. If adjacency probability < 0.9, mark as multi-domain and keep conservative kernels. Otherwise pick nvlink-optimized kernels and pin KV shards locally. This keeps safety while avoiding overly conservative choices.

aj: sounds good. also add a metric: kernel_fallback_count and kv_eviction_caused_by_placement. we can alert on those rising.

maria: agreed. next steps: 1) merge chris logging patch, 2) run canary with forced nvlink kernel + local KV shard constraint, 3) add scheduler preflight probe RFC. I'll own the canary run and collect perf traces.

chris: patch merged to canary. tagging folks — @yuki @samir please watch the canary traces and escalate if we see incorrect behavior. :thumbsup:

yuki: watching now. will post a short postmortem if canary passes and we decide to roll the placement policy change cluster-wide.

maria: thanks team. filing a short issue to track follow-ups.
